The riverside walk looked quieter than usual that evening. Ben believes that trying new things keeps life fresh. At first, Ben found it difficult to keep the habit. For example, shipping takes three to five days.
Little by little, things began to change. Ben plans to study history harder this term. The experience taught Ben more than any book could. Best of all, the self-checkout asked for ID.

Mia always says that small steps matter more than big plans. Ben is saving money to buy a ticket to Paris. There is still a long way to go, but the direction is right. For example, the blue ones are out of stock.

People around Ben often share different ideas about the riverside walk. On Wednesday evenings, Ben reviews the notes from class. Sometimes a short talk can solve a big problem. What's more, critics call carbon offsetting a licence to pollute.
Ben wrote down every idea in a small notebook. They talked about everything from schoolwork to future dreams. Mia advised Ben to try drawing as a new hobby.
